selectionRule: Minimize comfortable-win Top10 rank error with no worsening of overall error, Top25 overlap, big-drop error, or big-drop recall on 2019–2024. Fixed variants before running. 2025/2026 previously inspected follow-ups.
methodology: Big drop: previous AP Top10 team wins all games since previous poll, with at least one played, and drops >=3 places. False alarms measured among other winning Top10 cases.
2015+ history; evaluation 2019–2024 walk forward. 2025 and current 2026 are previously inspected follow-up data, not fresh holdouts.
Same AP/closing-Vegas inputs as earlier experiment, with normalized provider names. Historical closing lines lack independently verified quote timestamps.
Early-season features fade over first four games. Peers are teams up to five ranks above/below in the previous AP poll; context uses their known game margins, Vegas residuals, and ranked wins.
Nonlinear models learn change in normalized AP score from prior poll, using depth3 histogram trees, 100 rounds, rate0.05, minleaf45; all thresholds fitted on training only.

Weighted-movement model gives fourfold weight to all winning Top10 examples. Drop-weighted variant gives eightfold weight to historical big-drop labels in training seasons only, with minleaf20; the other nonlinear variants use minleaf45.
Rankings are recomputed across all candidates; no Oregon-specific adjustment or fixed drop rule.

Comfortable-win calibration: negative predicted movement is reduced linearly from zero adjustment at a 14-point minimum recent win to full adjustment at 42 points. Positive movement stays unchanged; rank can still fall as peers advance. Selected on 2019–2024; 2025 slightly worsens and is reported explicitly.
